resources.string: "If there is a bug in DistroHopper, that does not necessarily mean that I am aware of its existence. Developers are generally quite bad at testing their own applications as they will only use them in a way they are intended to be used. Some problems also only exist in certain specific circumstances (for example a certain device running a specific version of Android with some extra options enabled). So if you find a bug in DistroHopper (or if you have a feature request) you can help out by reporting it. Bug reports for DistroHopper are kept on GitHub. If GitHub is too technical for you, you can also just send an e-mail to android-dev@robinj.be. Just make sure it's in English or Dutch. Please provide as much (relevant) information as possible."
"A lot of time and hard work went into the development of this application. If you'd like to help out, there are several ways in which you can do so."

"DistroHopper is available in several languages. This is because volunteers provide the project with their translations. If DistroHopper has not been translated yet into your own language, and you understand English (and you have sufficient knowledge of the Linux desktop to understand some of the more Unity-related terms), then helping out with translations is a good way to help out. Translations for DistroHopper are managed on Transifex. All you need to do is request to join a translation team. After that I will approve your request and you are good to go."

"Are you a Linux/open-source enthusiast? Whether you are or not, if it seems cool to be able to have the Linux desktop on your Android device, then this app is what you're looking for. Currently there is a choice between Ubuntu's Unity desktop, elementary OS' Pantheon desktop, and Gnome. Missing your desktop of choice? Get in touch and if there's enough interest I might just add it 😉
Features include a couple of different themes, a search feature which allows you to search from a multitude of different search sources (both local and remote), and customisation options.
If you have any suggestions or feedback, feel free to get in touch. The project is open-source with the source code publicly available at https://github.com/RobinJ1995/DistroHopper. If you're less technically-inclined but would still like to contribute, you can join the project's translation team over at https://www.transifex.com/distrohopper/.
